title: Cell penetration of oxadiazole-containing macrocycles

metadata.authors: Huh, Sungjoon; Batistatou, Nefeli; Wang, Jing; Saunders, George J.; Kritzer, Joshua A.; Yudin, Andrei K.

source_summary: This study shows that oxadiazole-containing cyclic peptides can achieve high cellular penetration, as revealed by the Chloroalkane Penetration Assay, despite low passive membrane permeability, highlighting the complexity of designing cell-penetrant macrocycles.
abstract: Cellular permeability is an important property in drug discovery and biological probe design. Here we investigate the effect of oxadiazole grafts on cellular permeability using Chloroalkane Penetration Assay.           ,              Passive membrane permeability is an important property in drug discovery and biological probe design. To elucidate the cell-penetrating ability of oxadiazole-containing (Odz) peptides, we employed the Chloroalkane Penetration Assay. The present study demonstrates that Odz cyclic peptides can be highly cell-penetrant depending on the position of specific side chains and the chloroalkane tag. Solution NMR shows that Odz cyclic peptides adopt a β-turn conformation. However, despite observing high cell penetration, we observed low passive permeability in experiments with artificial membranes. These findings highlight the complexity of controlling cell penetration for conformationally sensitive macrocycles and suggest that Odz cyclic peptides may provide a framework for designing cell-penetrant cyclic peptides.
